I am thinking about this year the same way I did last year — wheat and maize, one after the other, like I have done for forty years. My 16.1 mu is not small, so I cannot skimp, but I also cannot waste money. My wife and I cannot do all the work ourselves at harvest, so I will hire the combine like always.

For wheat, I will plant an improved variety — Jimai or something similar that the dealer in town recommends. Everyone around me uses improved seed now, the old kinds give too little. I sow in early October after the maize comes off. I apply compound fertilizer (diammonium and urea) as base before ploughing, then topdress with urea at jointing in spring. Last year I used about two bags of compound (50 kg each) and one bag of urea per mu across the season. That gives me maybe 22 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, 6 kg of potassium per mu. I would rather put a little extra than see the wheat turn yellow. I irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling — the well is there, why not use it. I spray once for aphids and powdery mildew, sometimes twice if the weather is wet. I plough before wheat because the maize stubble needs to go under.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever my neighbor Lao Wang got good yield from last year. I sow right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no tillage, just direct into the stubble, saves time and diesel. I use one bag of compound as starter and topdress urea at big flare stage. Maize takes more nitrogen than wheat because it grows fast in hot weather. About 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. I irrigate once or twice depending on the summer rain — if July is dry I must water, maize tasseling without water is a disaster. I spray once for corn borer.

My wheat gives me around 450 kg per mu in a normal year, maize around 550 kg. Together that is my main income. Prices of fertilizer went up again, but I cannot cut back — the ground here needs feeding every season.
